plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden-rayed flower heads with dark, seed-packed centers. Whole fields of them turn to face the sun and glow across the summer countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (roughly July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Central and eastern North America, and farmland across Europe
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west during the day and swing back overnight. This heliotropism stops once the flower matures and settles facing east.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, aromatic mounds send up slender spikes of tiny, fragrant purple flowers. The blooms hum with bees and perfume the warm air of Mediterranean hillsides and cottage gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (about June to August), with late blooms into early September in cooler areas
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe, including southern France, and gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans used the herb to scent their baths.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: This Australian tree is covered in fluffy, golden pom-pom blooms that light up the late-winter bush. The flowers have a honey-sweet scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (about July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
